evidence: I'm sorry, Marcus. Taking a day off and having no one show up is really frustrating.
grades.reason: The agent apologized and specifically acknowledged the day off and the frustration, but did not revisit empathy later or when the customer sounded doubtful.

evidence: Let me confirm: your install was today between 8 and noon, and no technician arrived?
grades.reason: The agent confirmed the main facts but ignored the customer's $50 install fee concern and his question 'For when?'.

evidence: I'm going to get this rebooked for you right now.
I've done that on my end, so you don't need to call back to book it.
grades.reason: The agent took charge of the rebooking and said the customer need not call back, but did not own the fee concern, the credit, or a firm outcome.

evidence: I've put in a new booking. A technician will come out to you soon, and they'll reach out to confirm the time.
grades.reason: The agent gave no specific slot (tomorrow 8-10 am or Saturday 9-11 am), no $25 missed-appointment credit, no fee clarification or removal, no call-ahead note and no reference number, so the issue was not truly resolved.

evidence: So to recap, I've rebooked your installation, and a technician will contact you to confirm the time. Is there anything else I can help with?
Thanks for your patience, Marcus. Have a good afternoon.
grades.reason: The close was polite, with a recap and an offer of more help, but the recap was vague and left out the fee, credit and reference number, and the customer's open fee question went unaddressed.
